item.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
item.description: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

item.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
item.description: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

item.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades
item.description: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.

item.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
item.description: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

item.title: Businesses are getting tariff refunds. Why aren't consumers getting their cut?
item.description: A slew of American companies are getting billions of dollars back in tariff refunds after a Supreme Court ruling. Many consumers, though, may never get anything back.
